questions.stem: Which of the following does not progress to carcinoma?
questions.solutionHtml:
Bowenoid papulosis
  • Bowenoid papulosis is a sexually transmitted disease caused by human papillomavirus (HPV) that presents as red-brown papules in the genital area and does not progress to carcinoma.


Robbins & Cotran Pathologic Basis of Disease, 10th Edition, Page No. 970-71

questions.stem: A sexually active young man presented with multiple polypoid growths over his penis. Histopathological findings from an excised lesion show papillary architecture with acanthosis, hyperkeratosis and koilocytosis of squamous epithelium. What is the likely diagnosis?
questions.solutionHtml:
Condyloma accuminata
  • The given clinical history is suggestive of Condyloma accuminata.
  • It is a sexually transmitted infection caused by human papillomavirus (HPV) and commonly presents as multiple papillary growths on the penis, perineum, and perianal area.
  • Histologically, it shows papillary architecture with acanthosis, hyperkeratosis, and koilocytosis of squamous epithelium.


Robbins & Cotran Pathologic Basis of Disease, 10th Edition, Page No. 984
